terms.short: A plan for how the learning rate changes over training, usually a warmup followed by a decay.
terms.definition: Instead of one fixed step size, training ramps the learning rate up for a short warmup, then lowers it, often along a cosine curve. Think of driving: ease onto the road, cruise, then slow down to park precisely. The decay lets the model settle into a good minimum.

terms.short: Gradients that shrink toward zero (or blow up) as they pass back through many layers or time steps.
terms.definition: Backpropagation multiplies one factor per layer, so factors below 1 make early layers learn almost nothing and factors above 1 make training blow up. It is like a message whispered down a very long line. Good initialization, normalization, residual connections, gating and clipping are the standard fixes.

terms.short: A layer that standardizes each feature using the mean and variance of the current mini-batch.
terms.definition: During training it rescales every feature to mean 0 and variance 1 across the batch, then applies a learned scale and shift; at inference it uses running averages instead. It speeds up and stabilizes training, especially in CNNs, but behaves poorly with very small batches.

terms.short: A layer that standardizes each example's features on their own, independent of the batch.
terms.definition: LayerNorm takes one token's feature vector, subtracts its mean and divides by its standard deviation, then applies a learned gain and bias. RMSNorm is a cheaper variant that skips the mean and just divides by the root mean square. Because it never looks at other examples, it suits transformers and LLMs.

terms.short: A shortcut that adds a block's input to its output, y = x + F(x).
terms.definition: Each block learns only a correction on top of what it receives, and the shortcut gives gradients a direct path backward. It is like an express lane that bypasses every stop. Residual connections made 100+ layer networks trainable and are in every transformer block.

terms.short: A regularizer that randomly zeroes a fraction of units during training.
terms.definition: Each training step, every unit is switched off with probability p and the rest are scaled up, so the network cannot rely on any single path. Like a team that practices with random players missing, it learns redundant skills. Dropout is turned off at inference.

terms.short: A neural network that slides small learned filters over its input to detect local patterns.
terms.definition: The same small kernel is reused at every position (weight sharing), producing feature maps; stacked layers build from edges to textures to objects. This built-in sense of locality makes CNNs efficient for images, audio and other grid data.

terms.short: A network that reads a sequence one step at a time, carrying a hidden state as memory.
terms.definition: At each step the same cell combines the new input with its previous hidden state. Plain RNNs struggle with long-range dependencies because gradients vanish; LSTM and GRU cells add gates that control what to keep, write and forget. Transformers replaced them for most language tasks.

terms.short: A score from -1 to 1 measuring how closely two vectors point in the same direction.
terms.definition: It is the dot product divided by the product of the vectors' lengths, so it ignores size and looks only at direction. Two embeddings with cosine near 1 have similar meaning. For unit-length vectors it equals the plain dot product.

terms.short: An autoencoder whose encoder outputs a probability distribution, so new data can be sampled from its latent space.
terms.definition: The encoder predicts a mean and spread for a latent code, a sample is drawn with the reparameterization trick, and the decoder rebuilds the input. A KL penalty keeps the latent space smooth and close to a standard normal, so decoding random codes gives plausible new examples.

terms.short: A generator and a discriminator trained against each other: one forges samples, the other spots fakes.
terms.definition: The generator turns random noise into samples and improves by fooling the discriminator, which learns to tell real from fake. Like a counterfeiter and a detective pushing each other to improve, it produces sharp results, but training is unstable and can suffer mode collapse.

terms.short: A generative model that learns to reverse a gradual noising process, turning random noise into data.
terms.definition: Training adds noise to real examples step by step and teaches a network to predict that noise. Generation starts from pure noise and removes it a little at a time, often guided by a text prompt. It is like a sculptor revealing a statue from a block of static.
